what_this_is: A prepared same-campus resolution, unsigned. Publishing Milwaukee needs exactly one reviewed decision that two Hilton brands sharing 515 N Jefferson St are distinct businesses. The repository treats an unreviewed shared address as unresolved by design -- identity_resolutions.json's own note says the guard 'treats a shared address as UNREVIEWED, never as an automatic duplicate and never as an automatic pass' -- and it requires a reviewer_id. No agent may supply one.
why_it_blocks_publication: The base listing builder de-duplicates by street address unless a reviewed resolution names the pair. Without one it keeps Home2 Suites and drops Tru by Hilton Milwaukee Downtown, while the market hub, the downtown corridor page and the policy-comparison table all still link to the dropped profile. The build reports 1 warning and 3 broken internal links, and 'zero broken internal links' is a release gate. Milwaukee therefore stays published=false until this is reviewed.

measured_effect_of_reviewing_it.method: the resolution was injected in memory for one build; nothing was written

evidence.census_state: Both identities are IDENTITY_CONFIRMED in the committed 147-property census and BOTH are already flagged collision_state SHARED_ADDRESS -- the market factory saw this and recorded it rather than resolving it.
distinguishing_facts: two distinct Hilton property codes: MKESORU (Tru) and MKESUHT (Home2 Suites)
two distinct first-party property pages on hilton.com
two distinct pet policies, each read from its own page and approved separately by the founder in PTF-MILWAUKEE-FOUNDER-DECISION-036
a dual-brand tower is one building with two hotels; neither is a duplicate listing of the other
shared_facts: the same telephone number (4142408331), which a dual-brand property commonly shares
evidence.what_the_resolution_would_NOT_assert: Nothing about either property's pet policy. A same-campus resolution is an identity decision only.

identities.canonical_name: Home2 Suites by Hilton Milwaukee Downtown

proposed_resolution_record.evidence: Hilton publishes the two hotels as separate properties with separate property codes (MKESUHT and MKESORU) on separate first-party pages, and each states its own pet policy. They occupy one dual-brand building at 515 N Jefferson St. One address, two hotels -- neither is a duplicate of the other and neither may be merged or suppressed.
proposed_resolution_record.resolution_hash: <computed by publication_guard when the record is written>

how_to_apply: 1. Review the evidence above and decide whether these are two distinct hotels.
2. If yes: append the proposed record to launch_packages/pettripfinder/identity_resolutions.json with your reviewer_id and reviewed_at, and let publication_guard compute resolution_hash.

3. Move launch_packages/pettripfinder/milwaukee_publication_037/release_contract.milwaukee-wi.prepared.json to deploy/netlify/release_contracts/milwaukee-wi.json -- it is already calibrated to the published state and verified clean against the derivation while the flag was on.
4. Set published: true on launch_packages/pettripfinder/hotel_policy_facts_milwaukee-wi.json (publication_037 --apply does all of this and asserts no record changes while doing it).
5. Rebuild and confirm 2,178 pages, 425 sitemap routes, 0 broken links.
If no: the decision is equally usable -- one of the two identities is then a duplicate, and that is a census question rather than a publication one.
